source_text:
Fragmenta in Lucam
Τοῦ ∆αμασκηνοῦ.
95.233 Καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους τὸ Πνεῦμα κάτεισι. Θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ Θεὸς πῦρ
καταναλίσκον ἐστί. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο πυρὶ λέγεται βαπτίζειν ὁ Χριστὸς, ἐπειδὴ ἐν εἴδει πυρίνων
γλωττῶν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους αὐτοῦ μαθητὰς τὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ χάριν ἐξέχεεν, ἢ διὰ τὸ τοῦ
μέλλοντος πυρὸς κολαστικόν. Βάπτισμα γὰρ κἀκεῖνο τελευταῖον, οὐ σωτήριον, ἀλλὰ
τῆς μὲν κακίας ἀναιρετικόν· οὐκέτι γὰρ κακία καὶ ἁμαρτία πολιτεύεται· κολάζον δὲ
ἀτελεύτητα.
thought_title: The Spirit's descent and the two fires of Christ's baptism
orientation: John of Damascus opens his fragments on Luke with a brief note explaining why Christ is said to baptize with fire, first through the Spirit's descent at Pentecost and then through the final punishing fire.
pass_a_gloss: And upon the apostles the Spirit comes down. For he is God; and God is a consuming fire. Because of this Christ is said to baptize with fire, since in the form of fiery tongues upon his holy disciples he poured out the grace of Christ, or because of the punishing fire to come. For that baptism too is final, not saving, but destructive of evil; for no longer will evil and sin hold sway; but it punishes endlessly.

choices.english: Christ is said to baptize with fire
choices.why: Keeps the passive construction of λέγεται and the dative πυρὶ as instrumental 'with fire,' matching the source's focus on the saying about Christ.
rejected: Christ is said to baptize in fire
it is said that Christ baptizes with fire

choices.english: in the form of fiery tongues
choices.why: Renders εἴδει as 'form' and keeps the genitive πυρίνων γλωττῶν as 'fiery tongues,' per the glossary, preserving the visible mode of the Spirit's descent.
rejected: in the shape of tongues of fire

choices.english: he poured out the grace of Christ
choices.why: Keeps the aorist ἐξέχεεν as 'poured out' and the genitive τοῦ Χριστοῦ as 'of Christ,' preserving the source's explicit attribution of the grace to Christ.
rejected: the grace of Christ was poured out

choices.term: οὐ σωτήριον, ἀλλὰ τῆς μὲν κακίας ἀναιρετικόν
choices.english: not saving, but destructive of evil
choices.why: Preserves the μὲν...δὲ contrast and the genitive τῆς κακίας as 'of evil,' keeping the adjective ἀναιρετικόν as 'destructive' per the glossary sense.
rejected: not for salvation, but removing evil

choices.term: οὐκέτι γὰρ κακία καὶ ἁμαρτία πολιτεύεται
choices.english: for no longer do evil and sin hold sway
choices.why: Renders πολιτεύεται as 'hold sway' to capture the political metaphor of evil and sin no longer governing, and keeps the present tense and the compound subject.
rejected: for evil and sin no longer conduct themselves
for evil and sin are no longer active

choices.why: Keeps the participle κολάζον as a finite 'punishes' for natural English, and renders ἀτελεύτητα adverbially as 'endlessly' per the glossary, preserving the durative force.

pass_b_english: The Spirit also comes down upon the apostles. For the Spirit is God, and God is a consuming fire. This is why Christ is said to baptize with fire: because he poured out the grace of Christ upon his holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues, or because of the punishing nature of the fire to come. That final baptism is not saving, but destructive of evil—for no longer will evil and sin hold sway—yet the fire punishes endlessly.
